title: Make develop/deploy terminal outcomes and trust metrics reflect real preview readiness
description: Use snapshots, preview-readiness checks, and Prometheus metrics so develop/deploy tasks only end in success when the updated site is actually restartable and observable.
action: In backend/services/task_service.py, create a pre-task snapshot for develop_code with commit_message set to f"Pre-task snapshot for {task.id}" and persist pre_task_version in the task result; add a helper named _verify_preview_ready() that performs HTTP GET to http://127.0.0.1:{site.port}/ with timeout=2 seconds, max_attempts=10, and sleep_seconds=1 after site_service.restart_site() for both develop_code and deploy_local; treat any 2xx or 3xx response as preview_ready=true and any timeout, connection error, or final 5xx/4xx result after all retries as preview_ready=false; set TaskStatus.FAILED instead of TaskStatus.SUCCESS when restart or readiness verification fails; when develop_code completes successfully, create a post-task snapshot and store post_task_version in the final result; in backend/core/metrics.py, add Prometheus counters task_terminal_total{task_type,status}, preview_restart_fail_total, and site_rollbacks_total{outcome}; increment them from backend/services/task_service.py and backend/services/version_service.py.

convergence.definition_of_done: Develop and deploy tasks only end in success when preview restart and readiness checks pass, and trust-related terminal outcomes are exported as metrics.

files.change: Create pre/post snapshots, verify preview readiness, and fail terminal state when restart or readiness verification fails.
Verify preview readiness after restart_site() and fail instead of reporting success when readiness does not pass.
Increment site_rollbacks_total outcome counters from rollback success/failure paths.
Add task_terminal_total, preview_restart_fail_total, and site_rollbacks_total counters.
Add develop/deploy tests that assert failed preview readiness produces FAILED status and snapshot lineage in task results.
Add metrics assertions for new trust counters with the existing Prometheus test reset fixture.

implementation: Before running provider execution for develop_code, call version_service.create_snapshot() with commit_message f"Pre-task snapshot for {task.id}" and record the returned version number/id in the task result as pre_task_version.
Add _verify_preview_ready(site: Site) to backend/services/task_service.py and make it perform HTTP GET to http://127.0.0.1:{site.port}/ with timeout=2 seconds, max_attempts=10, and sleep_seconds=1.
Treat any 2xx or 3xx HTTP response from _verify_preview_ready() as preview_ready=true; treat timeout, connection error, or a final 4xx/5xx result after all retries as preview_ready=false.

Replace unconditional TaskStatus.SUCCESS writes in develop_code and deploy_local flows with branches that persist FAILED plus structured preview_restart/preview_ready errors when readiness does not pass.
After a successful develop_code run, create a second snapshot and record post_task_version in the final task result.

Define and increment task_terminal_total{task_type,status}, preview_restart_fail_total, and site_rollbacks_total{outcome}; add explicit pytest coverage that asserts counter increments for failed preview readiness and rollback outcomes.

success_metrics: FAILED status on preview readiness failure for develop_code and deploy_local
task_terminal_total and site_rollbacks_total increment in targeted metric tests

reference.pattern: Current task status updates and metrics exposure already exist

rationale.chosen_approach: This makes task truth and monitoring converge on the same real signals instead of layering a new workflow abstraction on top.
decision_factors: preview restart currently does not gate success
snapshot/rollback is already part of the product promise
rationale.tradeoffs: Task completion may become stricter and expose more failures, but those failures are exactly what phase 1 is supposed to surface truthfully.

risks: Do not leave partially written task results when preview verification fails after provider execution succeeds.
